title: Factors and Multiples
intro: Factors and multiples underpin a large share of SAT number questions — primes, GCF/LCM word problems, divisibility shortcuts and prime factorization all live here. Work through each topic, try the unsolved problems with the hint ladder, then take the 8-question topic test.

items.name: GCF from primes
items.formula: product of shared primes to the LOWEST power

items.name: LCM from primes
items.formula: product of all primes to the HIGHEST power

items.name: Primality test
items.formula: no prime ≤ √n divides n ⇒ n is prime

topics.name: Prime Numbers
topics.details: A prime number is a whole number greater than 1 with exactly two distinct factors: 1 and itself. The primes begin 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, … . Two is the only even prime — every other even number is divisible by 2, giving it a third factor. The number 1 is not prime (it has only one factor) and not composite. To test whether n is prime, check for divisibility by each prime up to √n; if none divides n, it is prime. On the SAT, primes appear in factoring, in “how many primes” counting, and in clever divisibility arguments.

solved.problem: Is 91 a prime number?
solved.solution: Test primes up to √91 ≈ 9.5, so check 2, 3, 5, 7. It is odd (not ÷2), digit sum 9+1=10 (not ÷3), does not end in 0/5 (not ÷5). But 91 = 7 × 13, so 7 divides it. Therefore 91 is NOT prime — it is composite.

solved.problem: How many prime numbers are there between 20 and 40?
solved.solution: List candidates and remove composites: 23 (prime), 29 (prime), 31 (prime), 37 (prime). The numbers 21=3×7, 25=5², 27=3³, 33=3×11, 35=5×7, 39=3×13 are composite. So there are 4 primes: 23, 29, 31, 37.

solved.problem: Why is 2 the only even prime number?
solved.solution: A prime has exactly two factors. Every even number is divisible by 2. For an even number greater than 2, the divisors include 1, 2 and the number itself — at least three factors — so it cannot be prime. Only 2 has exactly the two factors 1 and 2, making it the single even prime.

solved.problem: The sum of the first five prime numbers is what?
solved.solution: The first five primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 (remember to start at 2, and that 1 is not prime). Their sum is 2 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 11 = 28.

unsolved.problem: Is 143 a prime number?
hints: It is odd, digit sum 8 (not ÷3), and does not end in 0 or 5.

unsolved.problem: How many primes lie between 1 and 20?
hints: Remember 1 is not prime; start counting from 2.

unsolved.problem: p is a prime number and p + 2 is also prime. Give all such p below 10.
hints: These are called twin primes — pairs differing by 2.
Check whether p+2 is itself prime in each case (9 = 3×3 is not).

unsolved.problem: What is the largest prime number less than 50?
hints: Test 47 for divisibility by 2, 3, 5 — none divide it.

unsolved.problem: The product of two primes is 35. What are the two primes?
hints: 35 is odd, so neither prime is 2.
Factor 35 into a product of two numbers.

topics.name: Composite Numbers
topics.details: A composite number is a whole number greater than 1 that has more than two factors — that is, it can be divided evenly by some number other than 1 and itself. Examples are 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, … . Every whole number above 1 is either prime or composite; 1 is neither. A useful idea is the semiprime: a composite that is the product of exactly two primes (such as 6 = 2 × 3 or 9 = 3 × 3). The number of factors a composite has can be found from its prime factorization, a frequent SAT shortcut.

solved.problem: List all composite numbers between 10 and 20.
solved.solution: Check each: 11, 13, 17, 19 are prime. The rest have extra factors: 12, 14, 15, 16, 18 (and we exclude the primes). So the composites are 12, 14, 15, 16, 18.

solved.problem: How many factors does the composite number 12 have?
solved.solution: Factor pairs of 12: 1×12, 2×6, 3×4. Listing all divisors gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 — that is 6 factors. (Check via 12 = 2² × 3: number of factors = (2+1)(1+1) = 6.)

solved.problem: Which is the smallest composite number?
solved.solution: Start above 1. The number 2 and 3 are prime. The next whole number, 4 = 2 × 2, has factors 1, 2, 4 — three factors — so it is composite. The smallest composite number is 4.

solved.problem: Is 1 composite?
solved.solution: No. A composite number must have more than two factors. The number 1 has exactly one factor (itself), so it is neither prime nor composite. This special case is often tested.

unsolved.problem: How many composite numbers are there between 1 and 10?
hints: 1 is neither prime nor composite; ignore it.

unsolved.problem: Which number is composite: 29, 31, 33, 37?
hints: Three of these are prime; find the odd one out.
Test divisibility by 3 using digit sums.

unsolved.problem: Find the smallest composite number greater than 30.
A composite number equals the product of exactly two primes and is even and less than 10. What is it?
hints: Even means one prime factor is 2.
The number = 2 × (a prime), and is under 10.

unsolved.problem: How many factors does 16 have, and is it composite?
hints: More than two factors means composite.

topics.name: Prime Factorization
topics.details: Prime factorization expresses a number as a product of primes, for example 60 = 2² × 3 × 5. By the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic this expression is unique apart from order. Find it by repeatedly dividing out the smallest prime, or with a factor tree. Prime factorization powers many SAT shortcuts: the number of divisors equals the product of (each exponent + 1); GCF and LCM come straight from the shared and combined prime powers; and a perfect square has only even exponents. Writing a number in this form turns hard divisibility questions into simple bookkeeping with exponents.

solved.problem: Find the prime factorization of 84.
solved.solution: Divide out smallest primes: 84 ÷ 2 = 42, 42 ÷ 2 = 21, 21 ÷ 3 = 7, and 7 is prime. So 84 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7 = 2² × 3 × 7.

solved.problem: How many positive divisors does 72 have?
solved.solution: 72 = 2³ × 3². Add one to each exponent and multiply: (3+1)(2+1) = 4 × 3 = 12 divisors.

solved.problem: Is 200 a perfect square? Use prime factorization.
solved.solution: 200 = 2³ × 5². A perfect square needs every exponent even. Here the exponent of 2 is 3 (odd), so 200 is not a perfect square.

solved.problem: Express 360 as a product of primes.

unsolved.problem: Find the prime factorization of 126.
hints: Start by dividing by the smallest prime, 2.

unsolved.problem: How many positive divisors does 2³ × 5² have?
hints: Use the divisor-counting rule on the exponents.

unsolved.problem: What is the smallest number you can multiply 90 by to get a perfect square?
hints: A perfect square needs all even exponents; find the odd ones.

unsolved.problem: Find the prime factorization of 1000.
A number is 2⁴ × 3. How many of its divisors are even?
hints: Odd divisors use only the factor 3: that is 3⁰ and 3¹ → 2 of them.

topics.name: Greatest Common Factor (GCF)
topics.details: The greatest common factor (GCF, also HCF) of two numbers is the largest number that divides both. The cleanest method uses prime factorization: take each shared prime raised to its lowest power. For example 48 = 2⁴ × 3 and 60 = 2² × 3 × 5 share 2² × 3 = 12, so GCF = 12. The Euclidean algorithm (repeated remainders) is faster for large numbers. GCF answers “largest equal groups / biggest tile” word problems, and two numbers whose GCF is 1 are called coprime. Remember the identity GCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.

solved.problem: Find the GCF of 24 and 36.
solved.solution: Factor: 24 = 2³ × 3, 36 = 2² × 3². Take the lowest power of each shared prime: 2² × 3¹ = 4 × 3 = 12. So GCF = 12.

solved.problem: A florist has 30 roses and 45 tulips and wants identical bouquets using all flowers. What is the greatest number of bouquets?
solved.solution: The number of bouquets must divide both 30 and 45, so take the GCF. 30 = 2 × 3 × 5, 45 = 3² × 5; shared = 3 × 5 = 15. Greatest number of bouquets = 15.

solved.problem: Are 14 and 25 coprime?
solved.solution: 14 = 2 × 7 and 25 = 5². They share no prime factor, so their GCF is 1 — yes, 14 and 25 are coprime.

solved.problem: The GCF of two numbers is 6 and their LCM is 72. If one number is 24, find the other.
solved.solution: Use GCF × LCM = product: 6 × 72 = 432. The other number = 432 ÷ 24 = 18.

unsolved.problem: Find the GCF of 18 and 48.
hints: Write each as a product of primes.
Take the lowest power of each shared prime: 2¹ × 3¹.

unsolved.problem: Two ribbons of length 36 cm and 60 cm are cut into equal pieces with none left over. What is the greatest possible piece length?
Find the GCF of 17 and 51.
hints: Check whether the smaller divides the larger.
If one divides the other, the GCF is the smaller number.

unsolved.problem: The GCF of two numbers is 8 and one number is 8. What can the other number be (give the smallest above 8)?
hints: The other = 8k, and GCF(8, 8k) = 8 needs k to share no extra factor of… actually any multiple of 8 works for GCF 8 as long as it is a multiple of 8.
Smallest multiple of 8 greater than 8 is 16.

unsolved.problem: GCF × LCM of two numbers is 600 and their GCF is 10. What is their LCM?
hints: Use GCF × LCM = product of the numbers — here you are given GCF × LCM directly as 600? Re-read: product = 600.

topics.name: Least Common Multiple (LCM)
topics.details: The least common multiple (LCM) of two numbers is the smallest number both divide into. From prime factorization, take each prime raised to its highest power across the numbers: for 12 = 2² × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3², the LCM is 2² × 3² = 36. The LCM answers “when do events line up again” problems — bells ringing, lights flashing, schedules repeating. A reliable shortcut is LCM(a, b) = (a × b) ÷ GCF(a, b). For more than two numbers, build the LCM prime by prime, always keeping the highest exponent seen.

solved.problem: Find the LCM of 12 and 18.
solved.solution: Factor: 12 = 2² × 3, 18 = 2 × 3². Take the highest power of each prime: 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36. So LCM = 36.

solved.problem: Two bells ring every 8 and 12 minutes. If they ring together now, after how many minutes do they next ring together?
solved.solution: They coincide at the LCM of 8 and 12. 8 = 2³, 12 = 2² × 3, highest powers 2³ × 3 = 24. They ring together again after 24 minutes.

solved.problem: Find the LCM of 6 and 8 using the GCF shortcut.
Find the LCM of 4, 6 and 10.

unsolved.problem: Find the LCM of 9 and 15.
hints: Take the highest power of every prime that appears.

unsolved.problem: Hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns in packs of 8. What is the least number of each you must buy to have equal counts?
hints: You need a common multiple of 10 and 8.

unsolved.problem: Find the LCM of 7 and 11.
hints: They share no factors, so GCF = 1.
LCM of coprime numbers is their product.

unsolved.problem: Lights flash every 15, 30 and 45 seconds. When do all three flash together (after the start)?
The LCM of two numbers is 60 and their GCF is 5. If one number is 15, find the other.
hints: Use GCF × LCM = product of the numbers.

topics.name: Divisibility Rules
topics.details: Divisibility rules let you test factors without long division. A number is divisible by 2 if it ends in an even digit; by 3 if its digit sum is divisible by 3; by 4 if its last two digits form a multiple of 4; by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5; by 6 if it passes both the 2 and 3 tests; by 8 if its last three digits are a multiple of 8; by 9 if its digit sum is divisible by 9; by 10 if it ends in 0; and by 11 if the alternating digit sum is a multiple of 11. Combining rules (for 6, 12, 15, 18) is a common SAT move.

solved.problem: Is 4,572 divisible by 6?
solved.solution: Test 2 and 3. It ends in 2 (even) ✓. Digit sum 4+5+7+2 = 18, divisible by 3 ✓. Passing both, 4,572 is divisible by 6.

solved.problem: Is 8,135 divisible by 11?
solved.solution: Alternating sum from the right: 5 − 3 + 1 − 8 = −5. Since −5 is not a multiple of 11, 8,135 is NOT divisible by 11.

solved.problem: What digit d makes 23d divisible by 9?
solved.solution: Digit sum 2 + 3 + d = 5 + d must be a multiple of 9. The value 9 gives d = 4. So d = 4 (the number 234).

solved.problem: Is 7,128 divisible by 8?
solved.solution: Check the last three digits, 128. Since 128 = 8 × 16, it is a multiple of 8, so 7,128 is divisible by 8.

unsolved.problem: Is 3,456 divisible by 4?
hints: Only the last two digits matter for 4.

unsolved.problem: Is 1,234 divisible by 3?
What is the largest digit d so that 5,d2 (i.e. 5d2) is divisible by 6? Hint: it must be even already.
hints: It ends in 2, so the 2-test passes.
Need digit sum 5 + d + 2 = 7 + d divisible by 3.
Largest single digit d making 7+d a multiple of 3 is d = 8 (sum 15).

unsolved.problem: Is 90,909 divisible by 11?
hints: Take the alternating sum of digits.
unsolved.answer: No (27 is not a multiple of 11).

unsolved.problem: A number is divisible by both 5 and 9. What is the smallest 3-digit such number?
hints: Divisible by 5 and 9 means divisible by 45.

topics.name: Factor Trees
topics.details: A factor tree is a diagram for finding a prime factorization. Start with the number, split it into any factor pair, then keep splitting each composite branch until every leaf is prime. The product of all the leaves equals the original number, and the multiset of leaves is the same no matter which split you start with. For example, 36 → 6 × 6 → (2 × 3)(2 × 3) gives leaves 2, 2, 3, 3, so 36 = 2² × 3². Factor trees make the divisor-counting rule, GCF and LCM visual, and are an easy way to avoid arithmetic slips on the SAT.

solved.problem: Use a factor tree to find the prime factorization of 48.
The leaves of a factor tree are 2, 2, 3, 5. What number does the tree represent?
solved.solution: Multiply the leaves: 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60. The number is 60 (= 2² × 3 × 5).

solved.problem: A factor tree has five leaves, all equal to 2. What is the number and how many divisors does it have?
solved.solution: Five 2s multiply to 2⁵ = 32. Number of divisors = exponent + 1 = 5 + 1 = 6.

solved.problem: Two factor trees give leaves {2, 2, 3} and {2, 3, 3}. What is the GCF of the two numbers?
solved.solution: The numbers are 2² × 3 = 12 and 2 × 3² = 18. GCF takes lowest shared powers: 2¹ × 3¹ = 6.

unsolved.problem: A factor tree has leaves 2, 3, 3. What number is it, and what is its prime factorization?
hints: Group the repeated prime as a power.

unsolved.problem: Build a factor tree for 100 and list its prime leaves.
A factor tree for a number has leaves 2, 2, 2, 7. How many positive divisors does the number have?
hints: Multiply the leaves to get the number, or read off exponents.

unsolved.problem: The prime leaves of a factor tree are 3, 3, 3. What number and which power of 3 is it?
Two numbers have factor-tree leaves {2, 2, 5} and {2, 5, 5}. Find their LCM.
hints: LCM takes the highest power of each prime.
